doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Recordings and character of the Ferguson band
summary: Players thought the records poorly recorded, but Lanny remembers a loose, sensitive band.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well you guys put some good stuff on wax.
Yeah. No one was ever really happy about it.

Well the band, I mean we always thought it was poorly recorded. But they sent me a request for some comments on that Mosaic CD, and I sent it to them and they sent me a set of them as payment, gratitude, whatever, which I thought was wonderful. I don’t know if they re-mastered those or not, but I thought everybody came out very well.
Not with me. He was on before me.

Yeah, but Carmen was a good player. I was familiar with what he did. That band was a lot of fun. You know it was a very loose band, and people used to accuse it of being loud © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

and out of tune, but it really wasn’t. It had moments when it probably was, but most of the time it was a pretty sensitive band, and the guys all got along most of the time. But it was something that I’m glad I did. I don’t know if I’d want to — well I know I wouldn’t want to repeat it at my age now, but it was something that I’m glad I did.
